subject: Telemetry Broker: mini-bridge design & SIEM parity checklist
messages:

Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0000
Subject: Telemetry Broker: mini-bridge design & SIEM parity checklist

Hi Evan / Priya —

Following our call, attaching a lightweight proposal for a "telemetry broker" (mini-bridge) that lives in Novacorp's VPC and forwards structured telemetry from Redwood Private into your SIEM. The goal is minimal footprint, parity with hosted signals (alerts, traces, structured logs), and an acceptance checklist you can run during onboarding.

High-level notes:
- Broker sits in Novacorp VPC (customer-owned subnet) behind a bastion/ALB.
- Data path: Redwood agents -> broker (TLS mTLS) -> Novacorp HEC / Splunk / SIEM via local forwarder.
- Trace hooks: sampling headers and span_id propagated; we expose an audit-only span link in events.
- Redaction: PII and secrets filtered at ingestion based on agreed regex and field map.

I've included: telemetry-broker-diagram.png, siem-parity-checklist.xlsx, and a short auth spec (mini-bridge-auth-spec.md).

Ask: can your team validate the parity checklist items marked "Novacorp validate" and confirm any non-negotiable network constraints (e.g., fixed IPs, firewall maintenance windows)?

Proposed timeline:
- 12/15: confirm network constraints and retention requirements
- 12/20: deploy broker PoC in staging
- 01/06: parity test run and evidence package (sample events, traces, metrics)

Thanks — I know your audits team is on a tight cadence. If helpful we'll schedule a short runbook walkthrough next week.

—
Aisha Rahman
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

From: Evan Cho <security@novacorp.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <ops+audits@novacorp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 13:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Telemetry Broker: mini-bridge design & SIEM parity checklist

Thanks Aisha — quick read and a few clarifications from my side: 

1) IPing and firewall windows
We can reserve two elastic IPs in the telemetry subnet and open outbound to your broker's ALB during the PoC window. We cannot open wide ranges; please plan for fixed egress IPs.

2) Retention and evidence
Our compliance requires a 90-day raw-event retention snapshot for audit evidence. Parity tests should include a secure transfer of a redacted evidence bundle.

3) TLS / mTLS
We prefer mTLS with cert rotation via our internal vault. Can Redwood support a cert rotation hook (SIGHUP-style or API) so we can rotate without redeploy? See attached quick note.

4) Trace correlation
We need a deterministic way to map Redwood span ids to our SIEM correlation ids. Can you include a mapping field (redwood_span_id) in the forwarded event payload (not as header)?

We'll validate the checklist items and respond with a red/green matrix by EOD 12/16. Also looping in Logan (our SIEM lead) to confirm HEC capacity.

Onward,
Evan

Evan — appreciate the detail. A few implementation notes from the Redwood side: 

- Fixed IPs: we can bind a small fleet of proxy instances to your two elastic IPs for the PoC; we recommend a single active + one hot standby.

- Cert rotation: Redwood Private runtime supports an API-triggered cert update for the broker process (POST /v1/broker/certs) which swaps certs in-memory and signals the forwarding process to re-establish connections. We'll add a rotation guide to the runbook.

- redwood_span_id: we can include redwood_span_id in the event JSON under metadata.trace.redwood_span_id. For SIEM mapping we'll include a sample transformation in mini-bridge-auth-spec.md so your parser can index it as correlation_id.

- Backpressure and buffering: by default the broker persists to local encrypted buffer (configurable size) and will back off to disk when HEC is unavailable. For evidence capture we'll produce a gzipped sample bundle (redacted) with signed checksums.

We will:
- Deliver an updated diagram that shows the fixed IPs and standby nodes by 12/15.
- Populate the parity checklist with Redwood's expected pass criteria and sample event payloads by 12/16.

If Novacorp prefers an agent-side HEC push (no broker), call that out — we can map both, but broker gives tighter control on filtering/filter rules and retention alignment.

—
Kimberly Park
Director, Integrations — Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick confirmation from audits: 

- We can accept the redaction model described provided the regex/file map is agreed before PoC deploy.
- 90-day retention snapshot is acceptable, but Novacorp will request S3 encrypted transfer and will provide temporary credentials scoped to an "evidence" prefix for the transfer window.
- Please notify us 72 hours before a cert rotation event during the PoC; after production we'll set a rolling rotation cadence.

Action items for Redwood (Novacorp validation expected):
1) Updated diagram with fixed IPs and standby topology (due 12/15)
2) Parity checklist with sample events + expected SIEM mappings (due 12/16)
3) Runbook: cert rotation steps, buffer sizing guidance, and evidence transfer steps (due 12/20)

We'll assign an internal reviewer once the checklist lands. If all green we'll aim to start the staging run on 12/22.

Priya Singh
Head of Audits — Novacorp
